item.title: Re: CSS Theme
item.content:encoded:
This is… very unpleasant to look at, in that it literally hurts my eyes trying to read it. The predominance of green and brown — especially in the chosen hues — provides very little in the way of contrast, making it difficult to read even with a high screen brightness, and this is even worse for the links, which blend almost entirely into the background. This problem is exacerbated even further by the presence of any display night modes which filter out blue light, although admittedly that is not entirely the fault of the theme.

But accessibility issues aside, it's just… not a good aesthetic, especially where the sidebar is involved (keeping the background colors the same as the normal theme but completely inverting the text color was a really poor call). I don't really know how else to put it. It's not pretty to look at and is literally painful to read. I would seriously and strongly suggest you get in touch with someone with experience in graphic design and reevaluate some of the choices in your color palette and try to add more contrast between the text and the backgrounds. As it is, the theme at the moment is enough to turn me off from even attempting to read the other articles for this GOI.

item.title: Something That I //Just// Wanna Put Out There
item.content:encoded:
So, for all not in the know, I am taking a break from writing for the site. With that preface, I wanna say that if this doesn't follow through, then I have no room to complain, because clearly I am not writing the stuff, so. Anyways, the concern is just as follows:

+ show block
– hide block

I think that having Critter Profiles be the "official" GoI format of WWS would be a mistake. There is nothing wrong with them as an idea. While they are similar to the SCP format, there is a good reason for stuff like that. WWS, like SCP, is an organization dedicated to the containment and research of anomalies. Showing their similarities by a similar format also highlights their differences, because it clearly showcases their different approach to handling anomalies and their attitudes and such. However, I know a common complaint about GoI formats is that they are often just "redesigns" of the SCP format. Whereas I feel that is far more justified for WWS than some others, it is a valid complaint, and I would hate to see Critter Profiles become the official WWS GoI format. Not to say they can not exist. Clearly we can, we have them and they're good and staying in the positives. Just saying that we need some diversity.

If I was still writing, I would make this happen not by making a post but by writing something myself. As is, I am simply trying to promote some creativity surrounding WWS GoI formats.

To start a spark, here are some of my own ideas:

  • Adoption posters for odd specimens, think things like this and this.
  • A workplace calendar / assignment sheet, to give a look into day to day like working in WWS. What is commonplace and boring elsewhere could probably be quirked up in a setting like such.
  • What about public outreach? Connected with the community, WWS must put out some interesting calls for fundraisers, or "be on the lookout for this thing we are trying to capture but is currently on the loose!", maybe excepts from articles they put in the local newspaper. Calls for volunteers to help with various local projects, like cleaning up a river? Stuff like that.
  • Private property can be difficult to work around when needing to intrude (or take over) to do their job. I am not a legal expert, but I seem to remember there being some paperwork around stuff like this.
  • Probably many more things for the creative folks around here to think up.

As a courtesy to our mobile readers, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

Thank you, Zyn. Tired brain doesn't think of these things. ~DarkStuff

I feel a little weird posting this, as "guys people should make these things" is not a usually… good? Thing to do, and if you want to make things happen the best way to do it is usually to, you know, do it yourself. However, taking a break from the site, I am only hoping to inspire some people to get creative with what a GoI format can be, and take a good amount of liberties. Er, I guess that's all I got to say. Have fun doing this, or not! As I said, I ain't writing, so if it doesn't happen I have no room to complain.

item.title: Re: A question.
item.content:encoded:
No actual zoo, but they probably work in tandem with local animal shelters and can have tours where they show people animals they are rehabilitating (if they’re public-friendly). Anomalies are generally known, but mostly just that things around here are “a bit odd”.

For clarification, I would think that someone living in the town would sorta know about these things, but upon becoming part of Wilson’s Wildlife Solutions they would still be surprised at just how weird everything can get.

Note that they don’t have many facilities. Having a dedicated zoo would probably be out of their budget (or just too expensive and dangerous to be worth it even if they could do it).

item.title: A question.
item.content:encoded:
I love the idea of Wilson's Wildlife Solutions and I think I'd like to write something to be included in it. And I have a question about the organization:

Is the WWS the kind of organization to have a zoo or some other form of public building in order to showcase animals? I could see it going either way. The way I see it for the purposes of WWS, Boring is kinda like Sloth's Pit where anomalous stuff just kinda happens and everyone ignores it, but if that's not really how it is that's cool too.

item.title: I will respond...
item.content:encoded:
Okay so, because employee morale is very important, I imagine that they have meetings maybe twice a week where everyone says what’s going on and such. Like, feelings and official stuff alike. That’s sorta how I imagined it. If something is urgent or a project is getting worked on, emails are certainly common. They can also go and meet people where they usually work, but the point is I think they would try and do as much as possible in person. For general things, I also definitely imagine they use bulletins.

At the HQ, I imagine that in the lobby, if there is a job that needs to get done that’s not super urgent then someone with the knowledge might put up a notice that it needs to get done and what needs to get done and anyone may come and take a job from the bulletin and go do it. Very freeform, not super tech savvy environment. No forums, definitely emails.

item.title: Hey y'all!
item.content:encoded:
And we're live! This has been quite the journey getting Wilson's Wildlife Solutions off the ground, and I can't thank the community enough for this opportunity. I mean, I only had to write two articles, and it just sort of happened from there. In particular, though, I have to thank Rimple, because he gave me the beginnings of a draft that offhandedly mentioned "Wilson's Wildlife Solutions" just as a name for someone to call in SCP-3466. I took that and made it way, way bigger and weirder. So thank you! Thank you so much for that inspiration!

Anyways, I realize there is no "how to write us" section, and I thought about adding one, but I think the Introduction & What We're All About sections are that. They tell you all you need to know before writing, and the way they are narrated gives you the typical Wilson's Wildlife tone. Other than that, even though we may not have GoI Formats or tales yet — key word, "yet" — the hub is 100% functional.

Also, expect an add-on to the hub at some point. I have some stuff I am writing, but it's a bit too esoteric for a generalized hub, so I'm going to make it and have this hub be its parent page. I'll keep what it actually is as a surprise for once it is up, but expect some cool "bonus content" for this hub page at some point in the future.

Well… that's all I have to say right now! Yay for Wilson's Wildlife! Yay for the chance to make it a hub! Yay yay yay!!

SOME CREDITS:

  • Rimple = Making the name and writing a very rough draft that inspired this whole mess.
  • Weryllium = Naming MTF Beta-4 the Castaways (ha ha what a funny dude).
  • Captain Kirby = For writing the Boring Agreement Excerpt on this here hub!
  • MonkofYobani = For the slogan "Where All Critters Are Welcome".
  • stormbreath = For the CSS theme, co-made with myself (though Storm did much, much more work).
